method: このデッキは AJATT の MCD（Massive-Context Cloze Deletion）の文章でできています。ふだんは「読んで思い出す」で解きます。
表：ニュース・ウィキペディア・文学から取った本物の文章と、このデッキのために書いた文章（2〜5文）。覚える言葉は色つき。読み・英語・ヒントは出ない。読んで、意味と読みを思い出してからタップ。
設定 › 答え方 › 穴埋め にすると MCD の穴埋めになる。「語」カードは単語まるごとが穴（同じ言葉が二度出てくる文章では、両方とも空欄）。
「字」カードは単語の漢字ひとつが穴。〔 〕の読みを手がかりに、その字を思い出す（最初の文章で）。穴埋めと4択のときだけ出てくる（読んで思い出すでは休み。記録は消えない）。
ひとつの文章から何枚もカードができる（1枚に未知はひとつ）。慣れたら次の文章が開き、同じ言葉に別の文脈で出会う。
裏：ふりがな付きの全文、読み、品詞、日本語の説明。英語の意味、その文の英訳、漢字の形と意味、ほかの文章、出典はタップで開く。
裏の文章と日本語の説明は、言葉をタップすると意味が出る（回廊では覚えるにも保存できる）。タップは採点に入らず、予定も変わらない。
判定は「もう一度／思い出せた」の二つで十分（FSRS-6）。迷ったら「もう一度」。
N1〜N3 の札は、公開の JLPT 語彙リスト（open-anki-jlpt-decks 系、2010年以前の旧基準）による目安。JLPT は公式の語彙リストを出していない。リストに載っていない語には札がない。

cards.en: A sequence of numbers like 2, 4, 8, 16, in which the ratio between neighboring numbers is always the same, is called a geometric sequence. Each number is twice the one before it, so you can tell at once that the next one is 32.

words.defJa: 決まった順に数を並べたもの。

cards.ja: 1、3、5、7、9……のように、決まった規則で数を並べたものを数列という。この例では、どの数も前の数に2を足して作られている。高校の数学では、こうした規則を見抜き、何番目の数でもすぐに求められる式を立てる練習をする。
cards.en: Numbers lined up according to a fixed rule, like 1, 3, 5, 7, 9..., are called a sequence. In this example, each number is made by adding 2 to the one before. In high-school maths you practise spotting such rules and writing a formula that gives any term in the sequence at once.

words.defJa: 数列のいちばん最初の数。

cards.ja: 1、4、7、10と続く数列は、初項が1で、3ずつ増えていく等差数列だ。公差が3なので、第10項は1に3を9回足して28になる。最初の数と増え方さえわかれば、何番目の数でもすぐに求められる。
cards.en: The sequence 1, 4, 7, 10, … is an arithmetic sequence whose first term is 1 and which increases by 3 each time. Since the common difference is 3, the 10th term is 1 plus 3 added nine times, which is 28. As long as you know the first number and how it grows, you can quickly find any term.

cards.en: Consider a geometric sequence with first term 2 and common ratio 3. After 2 comes 6, then 18: you get each next number by multiplying the previous one by 3. By just the tenth term, the value exceeds thirty thousand.

cards.en: The lavish town hall built for show was nothing but a heavy waste of money for the town. The upkeep costs kept piling up, while the roads and schools that really needed repair were put off again and again. Residents' anger finally boiled over at the next election.

cards.ja: 祖母は昔から、無駄な費えを何より嫌った。破れた靴下は繕い、包装紙はきれいに畳んでしまっておく。そうして少しずつ蓄えたお金で、孫たちの学費を援助してくれたのだ。
cards.en: My grandmother always hated needless expense more than anything. She darned torn socks and folded wrapping paper neatly to keep. With the money she saved bit by bit that way, she helped pay for her grandchildren's schooling.

cards.ja: 年度末の三月三十一日、そのスーパーでは閉店後に従業員総出で棚卸を行う。棚に並んだ缶詰や調味料を一つずつ数え、帳簿上の在庫数と合っているかを確かめていくのだ。作業が終わったのは、日付が変わる直前だった。
cards.en: On March 31st, the end of the fiscal year, the whole staff of the supermarket does a stocktake after closing. They count every can and condiment on the shelves one by one, checking that the numbers match the stock on the books. The work wasn't finished until just before midnight.

cards.ja: 小さな雑貨店を営む友人は、毎月末に一人で棚卸をしている。売れ残りの多い商品がわかれば、翌月はその仕入れを減らす。地味な作業だが、店を続けていくうえで欠かせないのだという。
cards.en: A friend who runs a small general store does a stocktake on her own at the end of every month. If she finds items that are piling up unsold, she orders fewer of them the next month. It's dull work, she says, but essential to keeping the shop going.

words.defJa: 売るために持っている商品や材料。

cards.ja: 決算期末になると、倉庫の商品や原材料を一つずつ数え、帳簿の数字と照らし合わせる。こうして確定した在庫の金額は、貸借対照表に棚卸資産として計上される。
cards.en: At the end of the fiscal period, the goods and raw materials in the warehouse are counted one by one and checked against the figures in the books. The stock value fixed in this way is recorded on the balance sheet as inventory.

cards.ja: 今回は、国際秩序の変遷を、覇権の交代という観点から整理します。ある時代に経済力と軍事力で他国を圧倒する国家が現れると、その国の通貨や制度が事実上の標準として定着します。十九世紀の英国、第二次世界大戦後の米国が典型的な例です。ただし、その地位が永続するわけではないという点が重要で、財政の負担や新興国の台頭によって、優位は次第に失われていきます。本日扱う書籍は、こうした交代が生じる条件を、豊富な史料から読み解いています。
cards.en: This time I'll organize the shifts in the international order from the angle of changes in hegemony. When, in a given era, a state appears that overwhelms others in economic and military power, its currency and institutions take root as the de facto standard. Nineteenth-century Britain and America after the Second World War are typical examples. The important point, however, is that this position does not last forever: through fiscal burdens and the rise of emerging powers, its advantage is gradually lost. The book we're looking at today reads, from a wealth of historical sources, the conditions under which such changes occur.

cards.tipJa: 「覇権を握る」「覇権争い」の形でよく使う。
cards.enTarget: This time I'll organize the shifts in the international order from the angle of changes in hegemony.
ruby: するわけではないという

cards.ja: 生成AIの普及を背景に、先端半導体をめぐる各国の動きが活発になっている。AI向けチップの開発では米国企業が強みを持つ一方、最先端の製造は台湾の企業に大きく依存しているのが現状だ。こうした中、日本や欧州も補助金を投じて、国内での生産拠点づくりを急いでいる。専門家の間では、技術の覇権を一国が握り続けるのは難しいとの見方もある。各国の政策に応じて、供給網の形は今後も変わっていきそうだ。
cards.en: Against the backdrop of the spread of generative AI, countries are becoming more active over advanced semiconductors. In developing chips for AI, American companies hold the advantage, while the most advanced manufacturing currently relies heavily on a Taiwanese company. Amid this, Japan and Europe are also pouring in subsidies and hurrying to build production bases at home. Among experts, there is also the view that it is hard for one country to keep holding technological hegemony. The shape of supply chains looks set to keep changing in response to each country's policies.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: ニュースでは「技術覇権」「覇権を握る」のように硬い文脈で使う。
cards.enTarget: Among experts, there is also the view that it is hard for one country to keep holding technological hegemony.

cards.ja: インドの歴史をたどると、武力で広い地域をまとめた王は少なくない。アショーカ王もその一人だが、激しい戦争の後、仏教を深く信仰したと伝えられている。力だけで手に入れた覇権は、人の体を従わせても心までは従わせられない、一時の支配にすぎない。王が「法」による統治の大切さを記した文を岩や石の柱に刻ませ、各地に残したのは、そのことに気づいたからだろうか。戦に勝つことと国を長く保つことは、同じではないのである。
cards.en: Looking back over Indian history, there were not a few kings who united wide regions by force of arms. King Ashoka was one of them, but after a fierce war he is said to have become a devout believer in Buddhism. Hegemony gained by force alone is only a passing rule that can make people's bodies obey but not their hearts. Was it because he realized this that the king had texts on the importance of rule by the Dharma carved on rocks and stone pillars and left across his lands? Winning a war and keeping a country for a long time are not the same thing.

cards.tipJa: 武力による支配を言うやや硬い語。精神的な支配には使いにくい。
cards.enTarget: Hegemony gained by force alone is only a passing rule that can make people's bodies obey but not their hearts.

cards.en: When an overwhelmingly powerful country enforces the rules of free trade, as Britain did in the nineteenth century and the United States in the late twentieth, the world economy tends to be stable. This idea is called hegemonic stability theory.

cards.en: Doctor shortages at regional hospitals are severe, and there are now nights when they cannot accept emergency patients, and it is not unusual for ambulances to drive to the next city. It is a grave situation that bears directly on residents' lives.

cards.ja: 十年前と比べて、子どもたちが外で遊ぶ時間は半分近くに減ったという。体力の低下にもつながる由々しき問題として、教育委員会は放課後の校庭開放を広げる方針だ。
cards.en: Compared with ten years ago, the time children spend playing outside has reportedly fallen by nearly half. Seeing it as a serious problem that also leads to declining fitness, the board of education plans to open school playgrounds after school more widely.

cards.ja: 今日は、江戸幕府がペリーの来航をどう受け止めたか、という話をします。1853年、黒船が浦賀沖に現れると、幕府はこれを国の行く末に関わる由々しき事態と見ました。面白いのは、幕府がそれまでの慣例を破り、大名たちにまで広く意見を求めたことです。これが結果的に、幕府の権威を弱めるきっかけになったとも言われています。危機のときのリーダーの判断がその後の流れをどう変えるのか、一緒に考えていきましょう。
cards.en: Today I'll talk about how the Edo shogunate took the arrival of Perry. In 1853, when the Black Ships appeared off Uraga, the shogunate saw it as a grave situation bearing on the country's future. What's interesting is that the shogunate broke with past custom and widely sought opinions, even from the daimyo. It is also said that this ended up becoming a trigger that weakened the shogunate's authority. Let's think together about how a leader's judgment in a crisis changes the course of what follows.

cards.tipJa: 「由々しき事態」「由々しき問題」の形でほぼ決まって使う、硬い書き言葉。
cards.enTarget: In 1853, when the Black Ships appeared off Uraga, the shogunate saw it as a grave situation bearing on the country's future.
ruby: めるきっかけになったとも

cards.ja: 生成AIを使って作られた偽の音声や動画が、インターネット上で急速に広がっている。実在の人物が言ってもいないことを話しているように見せる手口もあり、本物かどうかを判断するのは専門家でも容易ではない。選挙や災害の際にこうした情報が拡散すれば、社会の信頼を損なう由々しき問題になりかねない。各国では、AIで作った映像や音声に表示を義務づける動きも出ている。技術の進歩にルールづくりが追いつけるかが問われている。
cards.en: Fake audio and video made with generative AI are spreading rapidly on the internet. Some tricks make a real person appear to say things they never said, and judging whether something is genuine is not easy even for experts. If such information spreads during elections or disasters, it could become a grave problem that damages trust in society. In various countries there are also moves to require labels on video and audio made with AI. The question is whether rule-making can keep up with the progress of technology.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 報道や公式の発言で、事の重大さを強調するときに使う。
cards.enTarget: If such information spreads during elections or disasters, it could become a grave problem that damages trust in society.

cards.ja: 私たちは、他人の小さな過ちにはすぐ気づくのに、自分の心に起きている変化にはなかなか気づかない。仏教の教えには、怒りや欲そのものよりも、それに気づかないまま流されていく心のほうを、由々しきこととして見る面がある。火は小さなうちなら手で消せるが、燃え広がってからでは遅い。だからこそ、一日の終わりに静かに座り、今日の自分の心をそっと振り返る時間を持ちたい。それは特別な修行ではなく、誰にでもできる小さな手入れなのである。
cards.en: We notice other people's small faults at once, yet we are slow to notice the changes taking place in our own minds. In the Buddhist teachings there is a side that regards as grave not so much anger or desire itself as the mind that is swept along without noticing them. A fire can be put out by hand while it is small, but once it has spread it is too late. That is exactly why I want to have time at the end of each day to sit quietly and gently look back on my mind. It is not a special practice but a small bit of upkeep that anyone can do.

cards.tipJa: 連体形「由々しき」で名詞を修飾する文語の名残。「由々しい」より改まった響き。
cards.enTarget: In the Buddhist teachings there is a side that regards as grave not so much anger or desire itself as the mind that is swept along without noticing them.
ruby: そのものよりも、それに

cards.ja: 国内シェアでは長年トップを守ってきたが、ここ数年は低価格を武器にした新興メーカーが急速に追い上げてきている。首位の座を守れるのか、社内には危機感が広がり始めた。
cards.en: The company has held the top domestic market share for years, but in the past few years upstart manufacturers armed with low prices have been rapidly closing in. Whether it can hold on to first place is unclear, and a sense of crisis has begun to spread within the company.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.enTarget: The company has held the top domestic market share for years, but in the past few years upstart manufacturers armed with low prices have been rapidly closing in.

cards.ja: 半導体の業界では、トップを走る企業がずっと安泰だとは限りません。技術の世代が一つ変わるたびに、後ろの企業が一気に差を詰めるチャンスが生まれるからです。実際、かつての首位企業が投資の判断を一度誤っただけで、後発組に追い上げられ、立場を失った例もあります。逆に言えば、先頭の企業ほど、常に次の一手を考え続けざるを得ないわけです。この緊張感こそが、業界全体の進歩を支えてきたと言えるでしょう。
cards.en: In the semiconductor industry, the company out in front is by no means guaranteed to stay safe forever. That's because each time the technology moves on a generation, a chance arises for those behind to close the gap in one go. In fact, there have been cases where a former leader misjudged a single investment decision, was closed in on by latecomers, and lost its position. Put the other way round, the company in front has no choice but to keep thinking about its next move. You could say this very tension is what has driven the progress of the whole industry.

cards.tipJa: 受け身「追い上げられる」は、先頭側が差を詰められて苦しい立場を表す。

cards.ja: 十九世紀の後半、産業革命の先頭を走っていたイギリスを、ドイツとアメリカが急速に追い上げた。両国は鉄鋼や化学、電気といった新しい分野に力を注ぎ、生産を大きく伸ばした。十九世紀の終わりまでには、工業生産の規模でアメリカがイギリスを上回っていた。先に工業化した国ほど古い設備を抱え、新しい技術への切り替えが遅れたとの指摘もある。後発の国が一気に差を詰める構図は、その後も形を変えて繰り返されている。
cards.en: In the second half of the nineteenth century, Germany and the United States rapidly closed in on Britain, which had led the Industrial Revolution. Both countries poured effort into new fields such as steel, chemicals and electricity, and greatly expanded their output. By the end of the nineteenth century, the United States had overtaken Britain in the scale of its industrial production. Some point out that the countries that industrialised first were saddled with older equipment and were slower to switch to new technologies. The pattern of latecomers rapidly closing the gap has repeated itself in different forms ever since.

cards.ja: 模試の判定が悪くても、そこで諦める必要はまったくありません。受験生の成績は、秋以降に大きく伸びることも珍しくないからです。特に、基礎をしっかり固めてから応用問題に移った人は、終盤になって一気に追い上げてくることがよくあります。焦って難しい問題集に手を出すことなく、まずは間違えた問題を解き直すところから始めましょう。最後に笑うのは、地道な復習を積み重ねた人です。
cards.en: Even if your mock exam rating is poor, there is absolutely no need to give up at that point. That's because it's not unusual for students' results to jump a great deal from autumn onward. In particular, people who firmly shore up the basics before moving on to applied problems often surge from behind in the final stretch. Without rushing to grab difficult problem books, start by reworking the problems you got wrong. The ones who laugh last are those who have steadily built up their review.

cards.ja: 会議とか勉強会で発言力の強い人が一人いると、その人が議論を全部牛耳っちゃうこと、ありますよね。で、周りは黙り込むんですけど、別に意見がないわけじゃないんですよ。心理学でいう同調圧力ってやつで、集団の中だと空気を読んで遠慮しちゃう傾向が強いらしくて。だから僕は、最初に匿名で意見を書き出してもらう方式を提案してるんです。そうすると、意外と鋭い指摘が出てきたりするんですよね。
cards.en: You know how, in meetings or study groups, if there's one person with a lot of clout, that person sometimes takes over the whole discussion? Then everyone else falls silent, but it's not like they have no opinions. It's what psychology calls conformity pressure: apparently, in a group there's a strong tendency to read the room and hold back. So what I suggest is a format where everyone first writes out their opinions anonymously. When you do that, surprisingly sharp points tend to come out.

cards.ja: 今回のテーマは、モンゴル帝国です。1206年にチンギス・ハンが草原の部族をまとめてから、わずか数十年のうちに、その支配は中国から東ヨーロッパにまで広がりました。この拡大のスピードは、世界史の中でもとにかく凄まじいものです。秘密は、馬を乗り継ぐ連絡網と、征服した土地の技術者を積極的に取り込む柔軟さにありました。強さの裏にある仕組みを、今日は順番に見ていきましょう。
cards.en: This time the theme is the Mongol Empire. Within just a few decades after Genghis Khan united the tribes of the steppe in 1206, its rule spread from China all the way to Eastern Europe. The speed of this expansion is truly tremendous, even within world history. The secret lay in a relay network of fresh horses and in the flexibility to actively take in engineers from the lands they conquered. Today let's look in order at the mechanisms behind that strength.

cards.ja: 生成AIの開発競争が続く中、データセンターの電力消費が急増している。大規模なAIモデルの学習には大量の半導体を長時間動かす必要があり、その電力需要の伸びは凄まじい。データセンターが集まる地域では、電力会社や各国政府が、発電所や送電網の整備を急いでいる。冷却に使う水の確保も、新たな課題として浮上している。省電力型のチップや新しい冷却技術の開発が、今後の鍵を握りそうだ。
cards.en: As the race to develop generative AI continues, the power consumption of data centers is soaring. Training large AI models requires running huge numbers of semiconductors for long periods, and the growth in that power demand is tremendous. In regions where data centers cluster, power companies and national governments are rushing to build up power plants and grids. Securing the water used for cooling has also emerged as a new challenge. The development of power-saving chips and new cooling technologies looks set to hold the key going forward.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.ja: このチームの守備のかなめは、キャプテンの佐藤選手だ。最後尾から声を出し続ける彼がいるからこそ、若い選手たちも落ち着いて動ける。けがで欠場した試合では、守りが崩れて大量失点した。
cards.en: The linchpin of this team's defense is the captain, Sato. It's because he keeps shouting instructions from the back that the young players can move calmly. In the match he missed through injury, the defense fell apart and they conceded a pile of goals.

cards.ja: 今日は、地図で見ればほんの小さな点にすぎない場所が、なぜ何百年も奪い合われてきたのかをお話しします。例えばジブラルタル海峡は、地中海と大西洋をつなぐ唯一の出入り口です。ここを押さえれば、行き来する船を一隻残らず見張ることができるわけです。つまり、海の交通のかなめを握った国が、貿易でも戦争でも優位に立てるということなんですね。地図を見るときは、海峡のような狭い水路に注目してみてください。
cards.en: Today I'll talk about why places that are no more than tiny dots when you look at a map have been fought over for hundreds of years. The Strait of Gibraltar, for example, is the only gateway linking the Mediterranean and the Atlantic. Hold it, and you can watch every single ship that comes and goes. In other words, the country that holds the linchpin of sea traffic gains the upper hand in both trade and war. When you look at a map, pay attention to narrow waterways such as straits.

cards.tipJa: 「〜のかなめ」「かなめを握る」の形で、全体を左右する一点を指す。漢字では「要」。

cards.ja: 扇は、根元のかなめ一本で何枚もの骨を束ねている。そこが緩めば、どれほど美しい絵が描かれていても、扇はたちまちばらばらになってしまう。仏教でいう戒も、案外これに似ているのかもしれない。一つ一つの決まりは細かく見えても、それらは散らばりやすい心を一点にまとめておくための留め具なのである。日々の暮らしが散らかって感じられるときは、自分を束ねている根元を確かめてみたい。
cards.en: A folding fan holds its many ribs together with a single pivot at the base. If that loosens, however beautiful the picture painted on it, the fan falls apart at once. The precepts of Buddhism may, surprisingly, be similar to this. Each rule may look petty, but together they are the clasp that keeps a mind prone to scattering gathered at one point. When daily life feels cluttered, I want to check the base that holds me together.

cards.ja: 半導体の工場でいちばん大事な数字は何かというと、実は歩留まりなんです。一枚のウエハーから何百個ものチップを切り出しますが、そのすべてが正しく動くわけではありません。目に見えないほど小さなほこりが一つ付いただけで、そのチップは不良品になってしまいます。同じ設備で同じ枚数を作っても、良品の割合が九割の工場と五割の工場とでは、利益がまるで違ってきます。だからこそ、各社はクリーンルームの管理に莫大なお金をかけているんですね。
cards.en: If you ask what the single most important number in a semiconductor plant is, it's actually the yield. Hundreds of chips are cut from a single wafer, but that doesn't mean every one of them works properly. A single speck of dust too small to see is enough to turn a chip into a reject. Even with the same equipment making the same number of wafers, a plant where nine in ten chips are good and one where only half are good make completely different profits. That's exactly why companies spend enormous sums keeping their clean rooms in order.

cards.ja: 先端半導体をめぐっては、各国が巨額の補助金を投じて国内への工場誘致を競っている。ただ、建物や装置はそろえられるものの、大量生産を軌道に乗せるのは容易ではない。新しい工場では当初、不良品が多く出て歩留まりが低い状態が続き、採算が合うまでに数年を要することも珍しくないという。専門家の間では、熟練した技術者をどれだけ確保できるかが成否を分けるとの見方が強い。工場の完成を伝える発表だけで、計画がうまくいったと判断するのは早計だと言えそうだ。
cards.en: Countries are competing to attract advanced chip plants to their own soil by pouring in huge subsidies. Yet although buildings and equipment can be put in place, getting mass production on track is no easy matter. At a new plant, many defective chips come off the line at first and the yield stays low, and it is said to be not unusual for it to take several years before the plant turns a profit. Among experts, the prevailing view is that success or failure hinges on how many skilled engineers can be secured. It would seem premature, then, to judge that such a plan has succeeded from announcements that a plant has been completed.

cards.en: Have you ever read three study guides only to find that very little of that knowledge was of use in the exam? If you look at how much actually stuck compared with how much you read, the proportion is surprisingly low. If you want to raise the yield of your studying, it is said to work better to spend time practising recall, even if that means cutting reading time. Rather than increasing input, increasing the number of times you pull things out of memory is the shortcut to forgetting less.

cards.ja: 最近のAIは、文章を書いたり絵を描いたりと、かなり高度な作業までこなすようになりました。でも、ここで一度立ち止まって押さえておきたいのは、AIが中身を理解しているかどうかは別の問題だということです。AIは大量のデータをもとに、次に来そうな言葉をとても上手に予測しています。人間の理解とどこが同じでどこが違うのか、それを考えることが、これからの時代の教養になっていくはずです。
cards.en: AI these days has come to handle some fairly advanced tasks, writing text and drawing pictures. But the thing I want you to stop and grasp here is that whether AI understands the content is a separate question. Based on vast amounts of data, AI is very good at predicting the word likely to come next. Thinking about where it is the same as human understanding and where it differs is surely going to become part of a well-rounded education in the years ahead.

cards.ja: 第二次世界大戦後、アメリカとソ連は、相手の国の様子を上空から写真に撮るため、特別な飛行機の開発を競った。撃ち落とされないためには、相手のミサイルが届かない高度を飛び続ける必要があった。空気の薄い上空でも安定して飛べるよう、設計にはさまざまな工夫が加えられた。しかしミサイルの性能が上がるにつれて、高く飛ぶだけでは安全とは言えなくなった。こうして、上空から情報を集める役目は、次第に人工衛星へと移った。
cards.en: After the Second World War, the United States and the Soviet Union competed to develop special aircraft to photograph each other's territory from the sky. To avoid being shot down, these planes had to keep flying at an altitude beyond the reach of the other side's missiles. Various ingenious features went into their design so that they could fly steadily even in the thin air at those heights. But as missiles grew more capable, flying high was no longer enough to be safe. And so the job of gathering information from above gradually passed to satellites.

cards.en: The ability to understand difficult teachings deeply is certainly admirable, yet being able to discuss advanced reasoning and being able to let go of the anger in front of you are entirely different matters. Once people learn difficult words, they easily feel as if that alone has lifted them a step higher. Buddhism has probably valued daily practice because it knew that people do not change through intellectual understanding alone. Knowing is no more than the entrance to the path. The walking is done, after all, with your own feet.

cards.ja: 今日は、アイデアを形にするときの話をしましょう。生成AIを使ったサービスは毎週のように発表されていますが、思いついた機能をそのままアプリに実装しても、使われるとは限りません。大事なのは、誰のどんな困りごとを解決するのかを先に決めることです。実際、うまくいっているサービスほど機能を絞り込み、本当に必要なものだけを残しています。機能を足すのではなく削って考える、これがポイントなんですね。
cards.en: Today let's talk about turning an idea into something real. New services built on generative AI are announced almost every week, but just building a feature you thought of straight into an app doesn't guarantee anyone will use it. What matters is deciding first whose problem, and what kind of problem, you're solving. In fact, the more successful a service is, the more it narrows down its features and keeps only what is truly needed. Thinking by cutting features rather than adding them is the key point.

cards.ja: 半導体の処理能力の向上は、これまで主に回路の微細化によって支えられてきた。しかし微細化のペースが鈍るにつれて、複数のチップを一つの基板の上にまとめて実装する技術に注目が集まっている。チップどうしをどう並べ、発生する熱をどう逃がすかが、製品全体の出来を左右するためだ。後工程と呼ばれるこの分野は、長く比較的地味な存在と見られてきた。ここにきて各国の政府や企業は、関連する投資を相次いで拡大している。
cards.en: Gains in semiconductor performance have so far been sustained mainly by making circuits ever smaller. But as the pace of miniaturisation slows, attention is turning to technology that mounts several chips together on a single substrate. That is because how the chips are arranged and how the heat they generate is drawn away decide the quality of the product as a whole. This field, known as back-end processing, had long been seen as a relatively unglamorous one. Now governments and companies in many countries are expanding related investment one after another.

cards.ja: 仏教の本はけっこう読んだんですけど、怒りを抑えるとか、執着を手放すとか、理屈としてはわかるじゃないですか。でも、それを自分の生活に実装できてるかっていうと、正直かなりあやしいんですよね。知識として蓄えておくだけじゃ意味がなくて、日々の些細な場面で実践を重ねることで、ようやく腑に落ちるんだと思います。満員電車で足を踏まれたとき、咄嗟にどう反応するか、とか。結局そういう瞬間に、本物かどうかが試されてる気がします。
cards.en: I've read quite a few books on Buddhism, and things like keeping your anger in check or letting go of attachment, you understand them in principle, right? But whether I've actually managed to implement that in my own life, honestly, that's pretty doubtful. I suspect just storing it up as knowledge is pointless, and it only truly clicks once you build up practice in the trivial moments of everyday life. Like how you react on the spot when someone steps on your foot on a packed train. In the end, I feel it's in moments like that that you're tested on whether it's real.

words.defJa: 電気や熱をよく通す物質。

cards.ja: 銅やアルミニウムのように電気をよく通す物質を導体という。反対に、ゴムやガラスのようにほとんど電気を通さない物質は絶縁体と呼ばれる。電線の芯に銅を使い、まわりをビニールで包むのはこのためだ。
cards.en: Substances that conduct electricity well, like copper and aluminium, are called conductors. Conversely, substances like rubber and glass that hardly conduct electricity at all are called insulators. That is why electric wires have a copper core wrapped in vinyl.

cards.ja: 濡れた手でコンセントやプラグに触ってはいけない、とよく言われる。人の体は水分を多く含み、電気を通しやすい導体だからだ。水で手が濡れていると皮膚の抵抗も下がり、感電の危険がいっそう高まる。
cards.en: We are often told not to touch sockets or plugs with wet hands. That is because the human body contains a lot of water and is a conductor that lets electricity through easily. When your hands are wet, the skin's resistance drops too, and the risk of electric shock rises even further.

words.defJa: 銅で作った細い線。

cards.ja: 工事現場から、ケーブルの中の銅線ばかりを狙った盗難が相次いでいる。銅の価格が上がったことで、盗んだ電線を業者に持ち込めば高値で売れるためだ。
cards.en: There has been a string of thefts from construction sites targeting just the copper wire inside cables. Because copper prices have risen, stolen wire fetches a high price when taken to a dealer.

cards.ja: 電線の中の銅は電気をよく通すが、そのまま触れると感電してしまう。そこで周りをゴムやビニールなどの絶縁体で覆い、電気が外に漏れないようにしている。
cards.en: The copper inside an electric wire conducts electricity well, but touch it bare and you get a shock. So it is covered in an insulator such as rubber or vinyl to keep the electricity from leaking out.

cards.ja: 石版印刷では、平らな石の表面に油性のクレヨンで直接絵を描く。水と油がはじき合う性質を利用して、描いた部分にだけインクをのせ、それを紙に刷り取るのだ。
cards.en: In lithography, you draw directly on the surface of a flat stone with an oily crayon. Using the way water and oil repel each other, ink is laid only on the drawn areas, and that is then printed onto paper.

cards.ja: デジタルカメラが普及する前は、撮り終えたフィルムを写真店に持っていき、現像を頼むのが当たり前だった。仕上がりは数日後で、どんな写真が撮れているか、受け取るまで分からないのも楽しみのひとつだった。
cards.en: Before digital cameras became common, it was normal to take a finished roll of film to a photo shop and have it developed. The prints were ready a few days later, and not knowing what kind of pictures you'd taken until you picked them up was part of the fun.

cards.ja: 大工の祖父がかんなを引くと、紙のように薄い木くずがくるくると丸まって床に落ちた。向こうが透けて見えるほどの削りこそ、腕の確かさの証しだという。

cards.ja: 老舗のそば屋では、だしに使う鰹節を毎朝その日の分だけかんなにかける。削りたての節は香りが立ち、袋入りのものとはまるで別物で、それが店の味を支えているという。
cards.en: At the long-established soba shop, each morning they plane just that day's worth of the dried bonito used for the broth. Freshly shaved bonito is fragrant, and they say it's nothing like the bagged kind; that, they say, is what underpins the shop's flavor.

cards.ja: 原油は、そのままではほとんど使い道がない。製油所では原油を加熱し、沸点の違いを利用して分留することで、ガソリンや灯油、軽油などに分けていく。

cards.ja: 工場のタンクでは、原料の液体が沈殿しないよう、底に取り付けた羽根で絶えず攪拌している。かき混ぜる速度が遅すぎると成分が分離し、製品の品質にむらが出てしまうからだ。

words.defJa: 物理や化学など、自然のしくみを研究する学問。

cards.ja: 理学と工学は似ているようで、目指すものが違う。前者は自然の仕組みそのものを解き明かそうとし、後者はその知識を使って、人の役に立つものを作ろうとする。

cards.en: My older sister, who discovered how fascinating physics is in high school, went straight into the science faculty at university without hesitation. cards.ja: 横浜や鎌倉、箱根など、神奈川県には人気の観光地が多い。東京から電車で一時間ほどで行けるため、週末になると日帰りの観光客で大いににぎわう。海と山の両方を一日で楽しめるのも魅力だ。
cards.en: Kanagawa Prefecture has many popular tourist spots, such as Yokohama, Kamakura and Hakone. Because you can get there in about an hour by train from Tokyo, they are crowded with day-trippers on weekends. Being able to enjoy both sea and mountains in a single day is part of the appeal.

cards.en: A schoolboy from the neighbourhood went missing after failing to come home from school. People from the neighbourhood association searched along the river and in the parks with torches until late at night. The next morning the boy was found asleep in a friend's shed.

words.defJa: 仕事のために勤め先へ行くこと。

cards.ja: 台風が近づいているため、会社は社員に自宅待機を指示した。それでも電車が動いているのを見て、律儀に出勤してきた新人が一人だけいて、部長は思わず苦笑いした。
cards.en: With a typhoon approaching, the company told its staff to stay at home. Even so, one conscientious new hire saw that the trains were running and came in to work anyway, and the department head couldn't help a wry smile.

cards.ja: どうやら父はフェアラムからの帰り、土地勘ない薄闇の田舎道で、白亜坑には囲いがなかったものですから、陪審はためらわず『事故死』の評決を。ぼくも死の事実関係をよくよく調べてみましたが、他殺をほのめかすようなものは何も見つかりません。争った形跡も、足跡もなく、強盗の線もなく、不審者の目撃証言もなし。
cards.en: It seems my father, on his way back from Fareham, was on an unfamiliar country lane in the dusk, and the chalk pit had no fence around it, so the jury unhesitatingly returned a verdict of 'accidental death'. I looked into the facts of his death thoroughly myself, but found nothing to hint at foul play. No signs of a struggle, no footprints, no sign of robbery, and no eyewitness reports of anyone suspicious.

words.defJa: 死刑の判決が決まり、刑を待っている人。

cards.ja: 判決が確定してから三十年近く、その死刑囚は拘置所の独房で再審を求め続けてきた。支援者たちは、当時の捜査に重大な誤りがあったと訴え、裁判のやり直しを求める署名を集めている。
cards.en: For nearly thirty years since his sentence became final, the death-row inmate has kept seeking a retrial from his solitary cell in the detention center. His supporters argue that the investigation at the time contained serious errors, and are collecting signatures calling for the case to be retried.

words.defJa: 東京都を受け持つ警察の本部。

cards.ja: 東京・渋谷のスクランブル交差点には、ハロウィーンの夜になると大勢の若者が集まる。警視庁は今年も数百人規模の警察官を動員し、事故やトラブルを防ぐための警備にあたる方針だ。

cards.ja: 都内では、息子や警察官を名乗る電話で現金をだまし取る詐欺が後を絶たない。警視庁は、電話でお金の話が出たらいったん切り、すぐに家族に相談するよう呼びかけている。

cards.en: In the Penal Code, "property" means things that have physical form and are of value to their owner, such as cash or jewellery. Intangible things like electricity are in principle not included, but the law contains a special provision for them.

words.defJa: 決まりを破った人への罰を定めた規則。

cards.ja: 改正条例の施行により、路上での喫煙が禁止される区域が広がった。違反した場合は二千円の過料が科される。市は「罰則を設けなければ実効性がない」として、巡回員による指導を強化する方針だ。
cards.en: With the amended ordinance in force, the zone where smoking on the street is banned has been widened. Violators will be fined 2,000 yen. The city says 'without a penalty it would have no teeth' and plans to step up guidance by patrol officers.

cards.en: The youngest member of the five-member idol group says that when they debuted, she struggled because she didn't know what her place in the group was. cards.en: Because of the heavy rain, a slope along a prefectural road in the mountains collapsed. The earth and rocks blocked the road, and the village farther in was temporarily cut off. cards.ja: 家を建てるとき、間取りの見た目ばかりに気を取られがちだが、大切なのは動線計画だ。台所から洗面所、物干し場までが一直線につながっていれば、毎日の家事はぐっと楽になる。

My art teacher used to say again and again, 'Don't be afraid of shadows.'

words.defJa: 性能や安全性を、実際に試して確かめること。

cards.ja: 自動運転バスの検証試験が、今月から市内の路線で始まった。運転席には安全のため係員が座り、歩行者の急な飛び出しや路上駐車にも正しく対応できるかを確かめる。結果がよければ、二年後の本格運行を目指す。
cards.en: A verification test of a self-driving bus began this month on a route in the city. For safety, a staff member sits in the driver's seat, and the test checks whether the bus responds correctly even to pedestrians suddenly stepping out or cars parked on the road. If the results are good, the aim is to start full service in two years.

cards.ja: アイデアが出ないとき、机にかじりついて考え続けるのは、かえって遠回りになることがあるそうです。心理学では、問題から一度離れている間に頭の中で整理が進む現象を「あたため」と呼んだりします。散歩の途中やシャワーを浴びているときに、ふと答えがひらめくのはそのためだと考えられています。ただし、その前に十分悩み抜いておくことが条件です。とことん考え抜いた上で休む、この順番が大事なんですね。
cards.en: When ideas won't come, staying glued to your desk and thinking on and on can apparently end up being the long way round. In psychology, the phenomenon in which things get sorted out in your head while you are away from a problem is sometimes called incubation. That is thought to be why an answer suddenly comes to you in the middle of a walk or while you are in the shower. The condition, though, is that you have wrestled with the problem thoroughly beforehand. Rest only after thinking it through completely: this order is what matters.

cards.ja: 蒸し暑い夏の夜、山の向こうの遠い空に稲妻がひらめいた。少し遅れて雷の音が届くころには、その光はもうどこにも見えない。古い仏教の教えには、この世のものごとを夢や稲妻にたとえる言葉がある。それは、消えていくものをただ悲しむのではなく、その一瞬の明るさを大切に受け止めなさい、ということなのだろう。人の一生もやはり、長い夜の中でたった一度だけ光る、あの稲妻のようなものなのかもしれない。
cards.en: On a sultry summer night, lightning flashed in the far sky beyond the mountains. By the time the sound of thunder arrived a little later, the light was nowhere to be seen. Among old Buddhist teachings there are words that liken the things of this world to dreams and lightning. That is probably telling us not simply to grieve over what fades away, but to take that moment's brightness to heart and treasure it. A human life, too, may after all be something like that lightning, shining just once in a long night.

cards.ja: AIに相談しながら企画を考えてると、急にいいアイデアがひらめくことってあるじゃないですか。あれって、AIが答えをくれたっていうより、質問を言葉にした時点で、頭の中が整理されてるんだと思うんですよね。だから、相手は別に人間でもいいし、ノートでもいいっていう。逆に、AIの答えをそのまま使うだけだと、自分の考えはあんまり育たない気がします。まあ、結局は使い方次第なんじゃないですかね。
cards.en: When you're working out a project while bouncing ideas off an AI, sometimes a good idea suddenly comes to you, right? I think that's less because the AI gave you the answer and more because your head gets sorted out the moment you put your question into words. So the other party could just as well be a person, or even a notebook. On the other hand, if you just use the AI's answer as it is, I feel your own thinking doesn't really grow. Well, in the end it comes down to how you use it, doesn't it?

cards.en: In robotics research, embodiment has been drawing renewed attention in recent years. That is because some intelligence is thought to be acquired only by actually moving a body, touching things and failing, rather than just calculating inside a head.

cards.ja: 書道の先生はよく「字は手で覚えるもの」と言う。筆の重さや紙の手ざわりを通して身につけた感覚は、頭で理解した知識よりずっと長く残る。学びにおける身体性とは、つまりそういうことなのだろう。
cards.en: My calligraphy teacher often says, 'You learn characters with your hand.' A feel acquired through the weight of the brush and the texture of the paper lasts far longer than knowledge understood in the head. That, I suppose, is what embodiment in learning means.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: とは、つまりそういうことなのだろう。

cards.ja: 今回のテーマは、AIに体は必要なのか、という問いです。いまの言語モデルは大量の文章から学びますが、コップの重さや水の冷たさを実際に感じたことはありません。そこで研究者の間では、知能には身体性が欠かせないのではないか、という議論が続いています。ロボットに手や目を持たせて、試行錯誤させる研究が増えているのはそのためです。言葉の意味は、体を通した経験に支えられているのかもしれませんね。
cards.en: This time's theme is the question of whether AI needs a body. Today's language models learn from huge amounts of text, but they have never actually felt the weight of a cup or the coldness of water. So among researchers there is an ongoing debate over whether embodiment might be indispensable to intelligence. That is why research that gives robots hands and eyes and lets them learn by trial and error is on the rise. The meaning of words may well be supported by experience gained through the body.

cards.ja: 仏教の修行では、心を整えようとする前に、まず姿勢と呼吸を整える。頭の中であれこれ考えるだけでは、心はなかなか静まらないからである。背筋を伸ばし、吐く息を長くするうちに、散らかっていた思いが少しずつ落ち着いていく。心の働きを体から切り離さないこの身体性こそが、坐禅という行の土台なのだろう。悟りもまた、本を読んで理解するものではなく、体ごと味わうものなのかもしれない。
cards.en: In Buddhist practice, before trying to settle the mind, one first settles posture and breathing. That is because the mind rarely grows still just by turning things over in one's head. As you straighten your back and lengthen each out-breath, scattered thoughts gradually calm down. It is probably this embodiment, which does not separate the workings of the mind from the body, that forms the foundation of the practice of zazen. Awakening, too, may be something to be tasted with the whole body rather than understood by reading books.

cards.en: This time, let's sort out the difference between Indian philosophy and Buddhism through the theme of the soul. In many schools of thought in ancient India, it was believed that even if the body perishes, the true self, the atman, remains without vanishing. This is the position known as the immortality of the soul. Buddhism, however, cast doubt on the very idea of an unchanging self. Although both grew from the same Indian soil, this is where the two clearly part ways.

cards.ja: 半導体の工場が一つ動き出すと、その周りには部品や薬品を扱う企業、物流の拠点などが集まってくる。熊本県では、台湾の半導体大手TSMCが中心となって建てた工場をきっかけに、周辺の地価や人手不足が大きな話題になった。工場の誘致は雇用を生むものの、人や車が一気に増えれば、道路の渋滞や住宅不足、地下水の確保といった課題は、わざわざ探さなくても自ずと浮かび上がる。自治体には、企業を呼び込むだけでなく、暮らしの側の備えも求められている。
cards.en: When a single semiconductor plant starts running, companies handling parts and chemicals, logistics hubs and the like gather around it. In Kumamoto Prefecture, a plant built mainly by the Taiwanese chip giant TSMC set off widespread discussion of nearby land prices and labor shortages. Attracting a plant creates jobs, but once people and cars increase all at once, issues such as traffic congestion, housing shortages and securing groundwater come to the surface naturally, without anyone having to go looking for them. Local governments are being asked not only to bring in companies but also to prepare on the side of everyday life.

cards.en: When you write about history, simply listing dates and events in order rarely leaves much in the reader's mind. What I'd recommend instead is a way of writing that focuses on a choice one person was forced to make. If you depict what that person knew and what they did not know, the atmosphere of the era comes across naturally. Rather than piling up explanations, by showing a single scene you get readers to start thinking for themselves. Once you've finished writing, read it back and check whether the character's hesitation comes through.

cards.ja: 言語学者チョムスキーは、人間には言葉を習得するための生得的な能力が備わっていると考えた。どの国の子どもも、ほぼ同じ時期に、ほぼ同じ順序で母語を身につけていくのはそのためだというのだ。
cards.en: The linguist Chomsky held that humans are born with an innate capacity for acquiring language. That, he argued, is why children in every country learn their mother tongue at about the same age and in about the same order.

cards.ja: 言語学者のチョムスキーが注目したのは、子どもが言葉を覚える速さでした。周りの大人が話す文には言い間違いも多く、子どもが受け取れる手がかりは限られています。それなのに、子どもはわずか数年で母語の複雑なルールを使いこなすようになります。そこで彼は、人間には言語を身につけるための生得的な仕組みが備わっていると考えたわけです。この考え方には今も賛否があって、そこが言語学の面白いところなんですね。
cards.en: What the linguist Chomsky focused on was how fast children learn language. The sentences the adults around them speak contain plenty of slips, and the clues a child can pick up are limited. Even so, within just a few years children come to handle the complex rules of their mother tongue. So he concluded that humans are equipped with an innate mechanism for acquiring language. This idea still divides opinion today, and that is exactly what makes linguistics interesting.

cards.ja: 大乗仏教には、生きとし生けるものはみな仏となる性質を宿している、という教えがある。それは修行によって外から付け加えるものではなく、はじめから内にあるものだとされる。もしそうなら、修行とは何かを新しく得ることではなく、曇った鏡を磨くことに近いのだろう。人の心に生得的な明るさがあると信じられるかどうかで、他人を見る目も変わってくる。厳しい言葉を投げる前に、その人の鏡がただ曇っているだけなのかもしれないと考えてみたい。
cards.en: Mahayana Buddhism teaches that every living being carries within it the nature to become a Buddha. That nature is said not to be something added from outside through practice, but something present within from the very beginning. If so, practice is less a matter of gaining something new than something close to polishing a clouded mirror. Whether we can believe there is an innate brightness in the human heart changes the way we look at others too. Before throwing harsh words at someone, I would like to stop and consider that their mirror may simply be clouded.

cards.ja: AIの研究では、どこまでを最初から組み込み、どこからをデータに学ばせるかがよく議論になります。人間の赤ちゃんも、顔らしい形に目を向けやすい傾向を持って生まれてくると言われています。こうした生得的な偏りが、その後の学習を進める上で、よい道しるべになっているわけです。勉強法に置きかえると、白紙から覚えるより、すでにある枠組みに結びつけたほうが定着しやすいということです。新しい単語も、知っている言葉と関連づけて覚えるのがおすすめです。
cards.en: In AI research, there is often debate over how much to build in from the start and how much to let the system learn from data. Human babies, too, are said to be born with a tendency to look toward face-like shapes. Innate biases like this serve as a useful guide as learning goes on. Translated into study methods, it means that things stick better when you tie them to a framework you already have than when you learn them from a blank slate. With new words, too, I recommend learning them by linking them to words you already know.

words.defJa: 目と脳で、見たものを処理するしくみ。

cards.ja: 目に入った光の情報は、網膜から視神経を通って脳の後ろのほうへ送られる。視覚系はそこで色や形、動きを別々に処理し、最後に一つの像としてまとめ上げている。
cards.en: Information from light entering the eye travels from the retina through the optic nerve to the back of the brain. There the visual system processes color, shape and motion separately and finally assembles them into a single image.

cards.ja: 錯視の図形を見ると、同じ長さの線が違う長さに見えてしまう。これは目の故障ではなく、視覚系が奥行きや周囲の手がかりから物の大きさを推測しているために起こる現象だ。
cards.en: When you look at an optical-illusion figure, lines of the same length look like different lengths. This isn't a fault in your eyes; it happens because the visual system estimates the size of things from depth and surrounding cues.

words.defJa: 強い磁場の中で原子核が電波に反応する現象。

cards.ja: MRIは、磁気共鳴という現象を利用して体の内部を画像にする検査だ。強い磁石と電波を使うため、X線検査のように被ばくする心配はないが、検査中はかなり大きな音がする。
cards.en: An MRI is a scan that images the inside of the body using the phenomenon of magnetic resonance. Because it uses a strong magnet and radio waves, there is no radiation exposure as with an X-ray, but it is quite loud during the scan.

cards.ja: 化学の研究室では、新しく合成した物質の構造を調べるのに核磁気共鳴装置を使う。強い磁場の中に試料を置き、原子核が電波にどう反応するかを測れば、分子の中で原子がどう並んでいるかがわかる。
cards.en: In chemistry labs, nuclear magnetic resonance instruments are used to determine the structure of newly synthesized substances. Place a sample in a strong magnetic field and measure how its nuclei respond to radio waves, and you can tell how the atoms are arranged in the molecule.

words.defJa: 磁石と電波で体の断面を画像にする検査。

cards.ja: 頭痛が続くため、父は病院で磁気共鳴断層撮影、いわゆるMRI検査を受けた。大きな磁石の筒の中に二十分ほど横になっていたが、工事のような音が響いて落ち着かなかったという。結果は異常なしだった。
cards.en: Because his headaches wouldn't go away, my father had magnetic resonance imaging, an MRI scan, at the hospital. He lay inside a big magnet tube for about twenty minutes, and said the construction-like noise made it hard to relax. The results showed nothing abnormal.

words.defJa: 耳の奥にあって、音で震えるうすい膜。

cards.ja: 耳の奥には、鼓膜と呼ばれる薄い膜が張られている。空気の振動が伝わるとこの膜が震え、その動きが奥にある小さな骨を通じて神経へと送られる。こうして私たちは音を聞いている。
cards.en: Deep inside the ear is a thin membrane called the eardrum. When vibrations in the air reach it, the membrane trembles, and that movement is passed through tiny bones behind it to the nerves. That is how we hear sound.

cards.ja: 山あいのこの村には診療所が一つしかなく、医師は週に二日しか来ない。急病のときは、車で一時間かけて町の病院まで行くしかない。過疎地の医療をどう守るかは、多くの自治体が抱える課題だ。
cards.en: This mountain village has only one clinic, and the doctor comes just two days a week. In an emergency, the only option is an hour's drive to the hospital in town. How to protect medical care in depopulated areas is a problem facing many local governments.

cards.ja: 夜中に娘が高い熱を出したので、急いで救急外来に連れていった。当直の医師は喉の奥をのぞき、胸に聴診器を当てて丁寧に診ると、「インフルエンザでしょう」と言って薬を出してくれた。
cards.en: In the middle of the night my daughter came down with a high fever, so I rushed her to the emergency department. The doctor on duty looked down her throat, put a stethoscope to her chest and examined her carefully, then said, 'It's probably flu,' and gave us some medicine.

cards.ja: 日本列島では、桜の開花は南から北へと進んでいく。毎年発表される開花日の分布図を見ると、春が少しずつ北上していく様子が手に取るようにわかる。北海道で桜が咲くのは、たいてい五月に入ってからだ。
cards.en: Across the Japanese archipelago, cherry blossoms open progressively from south to north. Looking at the map of blooming-date distribution published every year, you can see clearly how spring moves north little by little. In Hokkaido, the cherries usually don't bloom until May.

cards.ja: 満開の桜も、一週間もすれば雨と風に散ってしまう。その短い盛りに、昔の日本人は世の無常を重ね合わせてきた。花見のにぎわいの裏に、どこかもの悲しさが漂うのはそのためだろう。
cards.en: Even cherry trees in full bloom are scattered by rain and wind within a week. In that brief peak, the Japanese of old saw a reflection of the impermanence of the world. That is probably why a certain sadness hangs behind the merriment of blossom viewing.

cards.ja: いや、AIの世界って、去年の常識が今年にはもう陳腐化してたりするじゃないですか。半年前にがんばって覚えたツールの使い方が、定着する前に通用しなくなってたりして。そういうのを見てると、無常ってたぶんこういうことなのかなって、ちょっと思うんですよね。だから、新しく出てくるものを全部追いかけるのは、まあ無理なんですよ。状況は常に流動的だって最初から割り切っておいたほうが、気が楽になるんじゃないかなと。
cards.en: I mean, in the world of AI, last year's common sense has already gone stale by this year, right? The way you worked hard to learn a tool six months ago can stop working before it even becomes second nature. Watching that kind of thing, I sort of think, this is probably what impermanence means. So chasing everything new that comes out is, well, impossible. I think you'll feel more at ease if you accept from the start that the situation is always in flux.

cards.tipJa: くだけた会話では「〜って無常だなあ」と、軽い感慨としても使う。

cards.ja: 洗濯機の脱水は、遠心力を利用している。洗濯槽が高速で回ると、衣類に含まれた水が外側へと押し出され、槽の壁にある小さな穴から抜けていくのだ。回転が速いほど、衣類はよく乾く。
cards.en: A washing machine's spin cycle makes use of centrifugal force. When the drum spins at high speed, the water in the clothes is forced outward and escapes through the small holes in the drum wall. The faster it spins, the drier the clothes get.

cards.en: If you fill a bucket with water and swing it round vigorously, the water doesn't spill even when it's upside down. cards.ja: 足し算は「1を足す」操作の繰り返しで、掛け算は足し算の繰り返しで定義できる。このように、ごく簡単な関数から決まった規則で次々に組み立てられる関数を帰納的関数という。どんな関数なら計算できるのかを考える際の、出発点となる概念だ。
cards.en: Addition can be defined as repeating the operation "add 1", and multiplication as repeated addition. Functions built up step by step from very simple ones by fixed rules like this are called recursive functions. The concept is the starting point for asking which functions can be computed at all.

cards.ja: 機械学習の考え方を一言でまとめるなら、帰納的に学ぶ仕組みだと言えます。ルールを人間が一つずつ教えるのではなく、大量の例を見せて、そこから共通するパターンを見つけさせるわけです。猫の写真を何万枚も見せれば、AIは猫らしさの特徴を自分でつかんでいきます。ただし、例に偏りがあれば、引き出される結論もまた偏ってしまいます。データの質が大事だと言われるのは、そのためなんですね。
cards.en: If I had to sum up the idea behind machine learning in a word, it's a system that learns inductively. Instead of humans teaching it rules one by one, you show it a huge number of examples and have it find the patterns they share. Show it tens of thousands of cat photos and the AI picks up for itself the features that make a cat look like a cat. But if the examples are skewed, the conclusions drawn from them will be skewed too. That's why people say the quality of the data matters.

cards.ja: インドの論理学では、昔から「煙のあるところには火がある」という例がよく用いられてきた。かまどでも山火事でも、煙が立てば必ずそこに火があった。そうした経験を何度も重ねることで、人はそこから一つの法則を導き出す。だが、帰納的に得た結論は、どれほど確からしく見えても、次の一例によって覆されうる。確かさを求める心と、それを許さない世界とのあいだに、哲学は生まれるのかもしれない。
cards.en: Indian logic has long made frequent use of the example that where there is smoke, there is fire. Whether in a kitchen hearth or a forest fire, wherever smoke rose there was always fire. By accumulating such experiences again and again, people derive from them a general rule. Yet a conclusion reached inductively, however certain it may appear, can be overturned by the very next case. Perhaps philosophy is born in the gap between a mind that seeks certainty and a world that will not grant it.

cards.ja: 人間の言葉は曖昧さに満ちていて、一つの文に複数の解釈が成り立つことも珍しくない。その点、決定的文脈自由文法では、どの時点でも次に取るべき解析の手が一つに決まる。コンパイラが速く動くのは、この性質のおかげでもある。
cards.en: Human language is full of ambiguity, and it's not unusual for a single sentence to allow several interpretations. With a deterministic context-free grammar, by contrast, the next parsing step is fixed to a single choice at every point. This property is part of why compilers run fast.

cards.en: In my grandmother's kitchen, the first sound of the morning was katsuobushi being shaved on the plane. Freshly shaved flakes went into the pot, were brought to a quick boil and strained, and out came a fragrant dashi. Every day's miso soup started with that stock.

words.defJa: 香川県の名物で、こしが強いうどん。

cards.ja: 香川県は「うどん県」を名乗るほどのうどん好きの土地だ。こしの強い讃岐うどんを目当てに、朝から何軒もの店をはしごする観光客も珍しくない。一杯数百円という手ごろな値段も魅力だ。
cards.en: Kagawa loves udon so much that it calls itself 'Udon Prefecture'. It's not unusual for tourists to go from shop to shop from the morning on in search of firm, chewy Sanuki udon. The reasonable price of a few hundred yen a bowl is another attraction.

cards.ja: 高松の製麺所の片隅で、ゆでたての讃岐うどんに生卵としょうゆだけをかけてすする。もちもちとしたこしと小麦の香りが口いっぱいに広がり、シンプルさこそがいちばんのごちそうだと思い知らされる。
cards.en: In a corner of a noodle factory in Takamatsu, you slurp freshly boiled Sanuki udon topped with nothing but a raw egg and soy sauce. The springy texture and the aroma of wheat fill your mouth, and you realise that simplicity is the greatest treat of all.

words.defJa: 宿で、食事をつけずに泊まること。

cards.ja: 温泉街の旅館は一泊二食付きが基本だが、最近は素泊まりのプランを用意する宿も増えた。夕食は近くの居酒屋で地元の料理を楽しみ、宿には寝に帰るだけという旅も気軽でいい。
cards.en: Inns in hot-spring towns usually include dinner and breakfast, but more and more now offer room-only plans. Enjoying local food at a nearby izakaya for dinner and going back to the inn just to sleep makes for an easygoing trip.

words.defJa: 和室の奥の、掛け軸や花を飾る所。

cards.ja: 和室の床の間には、季節ごとに掛け軸を掛け替えるのが祖父の楽しみだった。正月には松の絵、夏には滝の絵。その下に一輪挿しを置くと、六畳の部屋がきりっと引き締まった。
cards.en: My grandfather loved changing the hanging scroll in the alcove of the tatami room with each season: a pine painting at New Year, a waterfall in summer. With a single-flower vase set beneath it, the six-mat room took on a crisp, composed air.

cards.ja: 戦前の日本では、中学校から上は男女別に学ぶのが当たり前だった。男子と女子が同じ教室で学ぶ共学が広まったのは、戦後の教育改革からである。今では、公立高校のほとんどが男女共に学ぶ学校になっている。
cards.en: In prewar Japan it was taken for granted that, from middle school up, boys and girls studied separately. It was only with the postwar education reforms that coeducation, with boys and girls learning in the same classroom, became widespread. Today, nearly all public high schools have boys and girls learning together.

words.defJa: 数字などの音を、別の言葉に当てること。

cards.ja: 年号や数字を覚えるとき、昔から頼りにされてきたのが語呂合わせだ。七九四年の平安京遷都は「鳴くよウグイス平安京」、ルート２は「一夜一夜に人見ごろ」。数字の羅列も、言葉に置き換えると不思議と忘れない。
cards.en: When it comes to memorizing dates and numbers, people have long relied on number puns. The move of the capital to Heian-kyō in 794 is "nakuyo uguisu Heian-kyō," and the square root of 2 is "hitoyo hitoyo ni hitomigoro." Even a string of digits sticks strangely well once you turn it into words.

words.defJa: 沖縄の言葉で、なんとかなるという意味。

cards.ja: 那覇の祖母は、私が受験に失敗して泣いていたとき、背中をさすりながら笑った。「なんくるないさ。まじめにやっていれば、道はちゃんと開けるよ」。あの一言に、何度救われたかわからない。
cards.en: When I was crying after failing my entrance exams, my grandmother in Naha rubbed my back and laughed. 'Nankuru nai sa — it'll all work out. If you keep doing things properly, the way will open up.' I can't count how many times those words have saved me.

cards.en: When you read modern translations of the sutras, I think you'll be surprised by how many parables there are. It goes like this: just as the lotus brings forth a pure flower from the mud, people too can awaken from within their delusions. Metaphors like these are a device for tying abstract teachings to everyday scenes. Taking home a single image sticks in memory more easily than memorizing difficult logic. In today's summary too, I'll make a point of valuing those images.

cards.en: With the spread of generative AI, demand for computing chips for data centers is expanding rapidly. Companies have announced the construction of new factories one after another, and the amount of investment is also rising sharply. On the other hand, the more demand swells as if a dam had burst, the more caution about the backlash that follows is indispensable. The market in this field has repeatedly gone through surges and slumps in demand in the past as well. Among experts, views are divided on how long the current wave will last.

cards.ja: 話がうまい人というと、立て板に水のごとく、よどみなく話す人を思い浮かべる方が多いでしょう。けれど、実際に聞き手の心に残るのは、むしろ間の取り方が上手な人だったりします。一文を短めに切り、相手がうなずいたり考えたりする時間をつくる。それだけで、同じ内容でも伝わり方は驚くほど変わります。話す速さではなく、相手の理解のペースに合わせて話すことを意識してみてください。
cards.en: When people think of a good speaker, many probably picture someone who talks without a hitch, like water poured down a propped-up board. But the ones who actually stay in listeners' hearts are often, if anything, people who are good at pausing. Cut each sentence on the short side and make time for the other person to nod or think. That alone changes how the same content comes across to a surprising degree. Try to be conscious of speaking not at a fast pace, but in step with the pace of the other person's understanding.

cards.tipJa: 「立て板に水のごとく」は慣用句。よどみなく話すさまを表す。

cards.ja: 本日は、法句経という古いお経から、怠けについての章を要約していきます。この章のキーワードは「放逸」、つまり、したい放題に流されて自分を律しない生き方のことで、これが修行の大きな敵とされているんです。面白いのは、悪いことをする前の段階として、だらけること自体を問題にしている点なんですね。ブッダが最期に弟子たちへ残したとされる言葉も、怠らずに励みなさいという内容でした。言ってみれば仏教は、日々の気の緩みから人生を見直す教えなんです。
cards.en: Today I'll summarize the chapter on laziness from an old scripture called the Dhammapada. The key word of this chapter is 'heedlessness', that is, a way of life that gets carried along by doing whatever one likes without disciplining oneself, and this is treated as a great enemy of practice. What's interesting is that it treats slacking itself as a problem, as a stage before doing anything bad. The words the Buddha is said to have left his disciples at the very end were also about striving without slacking. You could say Buddhism is a teaching that reexamines life starting from the small lapses of each day.

cards.ja: 欲しいものがすぐに手に入る時代は、ある意味で、放逸に生きることをずいぶんたやすくした。指先ひとつで食事も娯楽も家まで届き、我慢する場面はめっきり減っている。しかし、満たされるほど心が落ち着くかといえば、そうとは限らない。むしろ、ほどよい不便さの中でこそ、人は自分を整える力を育ててきたのではないか。便利さを手放す必要はないものの、それに使われない工夫は要るだろう。
cards.en: An age in which we can get what we want right away has, in a sense, made it much easier to live a self-indulgent life. Meals and entertainment arrive at our door at the touch of a finger, and the moments when we must hold back have sharply decreased. But it is not necessarily true that the more satisfied we are, the calmer the mind becomes. Rather, wasn't it within a moderate inconvenience that people have grown the power to put themselves in order? There is no need to give up convenience, but some effort not to be used by it is surely required.

cards.ja: ブッダの生涯をざっくりまとめると、最初の大きな転機は、何不自由ない暮らしを捨てた出家です。王子として生まれた彼は、国を継いでほしいという父の期待に背き、城を出ていきました。ここ、現代の感覚だとただの家出に見えるかもしれません。でも本人にとっては、老いや病、死という苦しみの答えを探すための、避けられない選択だったわけです。そう考えると、この決断の重さがぐっと伝わってくると思います。
cards.en: To summarize the Buddha's life roughly, the first big turning point is his renunciation, in which he gave up a life that lacked nothing. Born a prince, he went against his father's hope that he would inherit the kingdom, and left the palace. By modern standards, this might look like simply running away from home. But for him, it was an unavoidable choice made in order to search for an answer to the suffering of old age, sickness and death. Thinking of it that way, I think the weight of this decision really comes across.

cards.ja: 条約は、国と国との約束を文書にしたものである。しかし国内の法律と違い、国際社会には違反を強制的に取り締まる警察のような存在がない。そのため、ある国が合意に背く行動を取っても、他国が取れる手段は経済制裁や外交上の抗議などに限られる。こうした仕組みの弱さは、近代以降の国際関係において繰り返し議論されてきた。条約の実効性は、最終的には各国の信頼関係に支えられていると言える。
cards.en: A treaty is a promise between nations put into writing. But unlike domestic law, international society has no police-like body that forcibly cracks down on violations. Therefore, even if a country takes action that goes against an agreement, the means other countries can take are limited to things like economic sanctions and diplomatic protests. This weakness of the system has been debated repeatedly in international relations since the modern era. It can be said that the effectiveness of treaties is, in the end, supported by trust among nations.

cards.tipJa: 報道では「合意に背く」「国際法に背く」など、約束や規範を破る意味で使う。

cards.ja: 勉強の計画を立てても、なかなかその通りに進まないことってありますよね。実は、自分で決めたルールに背いてしまうのは、意志が弱いからとは限りません。そもそも計画が細かすぎて、少しのずれで全体が崩れる作りになっている場合が多いんです。多少遅れても立て直せるように、最初から週に一度は予備の時間を組み込んでおきましょう。完璧な計画よりも、崩れても戻れる計画を目指すのがコツです。
cards.en: Even when you make a study plan, it often doesn't go quite as planned, right? Actually, going against the rules you set for yourself isn't necessarily because your willpower is weak. In many cases, the plan is too detailed in the first place and built so that a small slip makes the whole thing collapse. Build in spare time at least once a week from the start so that you can recover even if you fall a little behind. The trick is to aim not for a perfect plan, but for one you can return to even when it breaks down.

cards.ja: その古い屋敷には、昔から不思議な噂が纏わりついている。夜になると、誰もいないはずの二階から足音が聞こえるというのだ。そのせいか、何年も買い手がつかないまま空き家になっている。
cards.en: Strange rumors have long clung to that old mansion. They say that at night you can hear footsteps from the second floor, where no one should be. Perhaps because of that, it has stood empty for years without a buyer.
